clue.text: Northern joke in lavatory, told in the distant past

indicators.note: the joke and the northern letter sit inside the lavatory word, which wraps around them

parts.note: loo is everyday British slang for a toilet
standard abbreviation for northern
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A northern comic tells an old toilet joke, a story from yesteryear.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo is everyday British slang for a toilet; 'told' is just a joining word, not a homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an adverbial meaning many years before now, matching the clue's phrase about remote former times.

clue.text: Bobby gets new leader for this influential group

indicators.note: a new leader means the opening letter of the policeman word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: taken as written; a bobby is a British policeman
the replacement first letter

explanation.surface: A police officer seems to be promoted under fresh leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: The B at the front of BOBBY is replaced by L, giving LOBBY.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobby is a pressure group trying to sway politicians, hence an influential group of campaigners.

clue.text: Open common

definitions.meaning: first meaning: unaffected and frank in manner
second meaning: ordinary, to be expected

explanation.walkthrough: Two bare adjectives, each a separate sense of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural behaviour is unaffected and frank, and something natural is ordinary or usual, as in 'it is natural to worry'.

clue.text: On top of that, one joins an orchestra

parts.note: a, the indefinite article, means one
the London Symphony Orchestra

explanation.surface: A newcomer signs up with an orchestra, in addition to other commitments.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are adverbs meaning in addition, besides, as well as what was already mentioned.

clue.text: Easily proved lawsuit, done at the start of the holiday period

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a legal matter so clear it is settled at once

definitions.text: done at the start of the holiday period
definitions.note: a cryptic description: what happens to a suitcase when packing, not a noun phrase
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read literally: a suitcase is opened and then shut when you pack for a trip

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal reading: a case (suitcase) that is opened and then shut as the holidays begin.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a legal matter or argument so clear-cut that its outcome is certain and needs little proof.

clue.text: Cul-de-sac that is limiting motorway flow

indicators.note: to limit something is to hem it in, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: i.e., id est, Latin for that is
M as in M1, the British motorway prefix
to pass is to go along or move through

explanation.surface: A dead-end road which is restricting the traffic flow on a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that is' reads as a link phrase, but it is the Latin abbreviation i.e., which wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cul-de-sac is a dead end, and figuratively an impasse is a deadlock with no way forward.

clue.text: Straight, fashionable request for dessert

parts.note: in means in fashion
a classic pudding
an order is a request, as in a restaurant

explanation.surface: Someone trendy asks the waiter for a pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'order for dessert' naturally, but in the answer the dessert comes before the order.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means perfectly neat and tidy, and straight here is the adjective for things put tidily in place.

clue.text: Fussy individual

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hard to please, exacting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fussy individual' reads as a noun phrase for a picky person, but both words are adjectives with separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A particular eater is choosy and demanding, while a particular item is one specific thing singled out from others.

clue.text: Nearly rescue female newsreader found in open grassland

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the rescue word loses its final letter

parts.note: to save is to rescue
Anna Ford, a well-known British television newsreader

explanation.surface: A woman presenting the news is almost saved after being found lost in the wild plains.
explanation.walkthrough: Anna Ford read the BBC and ITN news for many years, so crosswords use her as the newsreader.
explanation.definitionFit: A savanna is a broad tropical plain of grass with scattered trees, so it is wide open grassland.

clue.text: Ghastly red nose and back

indicators.note: something ghastly is horribly disfigured, so the letters come out mangled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unpleasant red nose and a sore back, a catalogue of ailments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like a body part to go with the nose, but it is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a proposal or candidate is to support or approve it publicly, exactly what endorsing means.

clue.text: King David's wife hath babes butchered

indicators.note: butchered means hacked to pieces, so the letters are chopped up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim biblical-sounding report that a queen's infants have been slaughtered.
explanation.walkthrough: The archaic 'hath' fits the Old Testament surface while supplying letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Bathsheba was the wife of Uriah whom David took as his own, and she became the mother of Solomon.

clue.text: Went mad, having left to go round the avenue

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: a red is a left-winger
Av. is the abbreviation for avenue

explanation.surface: Someone lost their wits after walking off around the boulevard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb of departure; here it is the political left, a red.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave is to talk wildly or deliriously, as one does when out of one's mind, so the past tense matches went mad.

clue.text: Horse-drawn cart turns round in this area

indicators.note: a cart that turns round faces the other way, so its word is read backwards

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads, traditionally for brewers

explanation.surface: A horse and cart wheels about in a confined space.
explanation.definitionFit: A yard is an enclosed piece of ground beside a building, an area for work or storage.

clue.text: Activist waving a magic pen in front of the Queen

indicators.note: waving something about sets it moving every which way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
R for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A protester brandishes a wand-like pen before the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A campaigner works actively for a social or political cause, which is what an activist does.

clue.text: Protects cooling system against discharges, we hear

definitions.note: a description of what the answer does; the answer is a noun

parts.note: anti means opposed to

indicators.note: what we hear is the spoken sound of the word for discharges, spelt differently

parts.note: to discharge someone is to release or let them go

explanation.surface: A legal-sounding note that cooling systems are guarded against releases.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the job of the substance rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antifreeze is added to an engine's coolant to stop it freezing in winter, so it keeps the radiator safe.

clue.text: Duplicated CD includes single

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it within, so the disc letters enclose the other word

parts.note: taken as written
lone means single, solitary

explanation.surface: A pirated compact disc has a hit single on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'CD' and 'single' both suggest music releases, but CD is just the two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To clone something is to make an exact copy of it, so cloned means copied or duplicated.

clue.text: Compete with flightless bird, getting behind

parts.note: the large Australian bird that cannot fly
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: A runner tries to race a bird that cannot fly and still falls behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To emulate someone is to try to equal or rival them, which is to strive to match or compete with them.

clue.text: Unfeeling kiss, holding it back

indicators.note: holding something means keeping it inside, so the kiss word wraps around the other

parts.note: a brush of the lips is a light kiss

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the little pronoun is written backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cold kiss in which one partner holds back.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutish means coarse, cruel and animal-like, lacking sensitivity, so it fits unfeeling.

clue.text: Churchman in essence needing sheets and blankets

indicators.note: the churchman is placed inside the essence word

parts.note: one's being is one's essential nature
Doctor of Divinity, a churchman's degree

explanation.surface: A clergyman, in his very nature, requires bed linen.
explanation.walkthrough: DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a clergyman in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedding is the collective name for the linen and covers put on a bed, such as sheets, blankets and pillows.

clue.text: Pawnbroker, one spiritually impure

parts.note: old slang: goods pawned are 'at my uncle's'
an, the article, means one

explanation.surface: A moneylender is declared morally tainted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle' is old British slang for a pawnbroker.
explanation.definitionFit: Unclean in a religious sense means ritually defiled or impure, not fit for worship.

clue.text: I'm taking ages to produce likenesses

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A portrait painter apologises for working so slowly.
explanation.definitionFit: Images are pictures or representations, which is what likenesses of a person or thing are.

clue.text: More useless European Member of Parliament has row

parts.note: standard abbreviation for European
standard abbreviation
a tier is a row of seats, one above another

explanation.surface: A Euro-politician gets into an argument, proving ever more ineffective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel, but here it is a row of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Emptier means more void of content or meaning, so more futile and useless, as with an emptier promise.

clue.text: Code breaking and helping to get a medal

indicators.note: breaking a code means cracking it open, so its letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a ration is a portion or helping

explanation.surface: A wartime codebreaker is decorated for services to the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helping' looks like assistance in the codebreaking story, but it is a serving of food.
explanation.definitionFit: A decoration is an honour such as a medal or order awarded for service or bravery.

clue.text: Start steak pudding and potato

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: its opening letter
pud is the informal British short form of pudding

explanation.surface: A menu of steak pudding with potatoes on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Steak pudding is a British suet dish, which makes 'steak pudding' look like one item.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is informal slang for a potato, used widely in Britain and Ireland.

clue.text: Dame Judi rests in a wooden chair

indicators.note: the name rests inside the following words, sitting across their join

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A famous actress relaxes in a wooden seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Judi Dench is the British actress made a Dame, known for Shakespeare roles and as M in the Bond films.

clue.text: Blackleg arrives in second taxi

parts.note: standard abbreviation for second
a cab is a taxi

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker turns up at work in a second taxi.
explanation.walkthrough: A blackleg is British slang for a worker who crosses a picket line during a strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Scab and blackleg are both contemptuous terms for a worker who refuses to join a strike or takes a striker's place.

clue.text: Some desire newly-weds and Soames desired her!

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the name is a portion of those words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A literary aside about longing, marriage and a character who coveted his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: In Galsworthy's Forsyte Saga, Soames Forsyte marries Irene and is obsessed with possessing her; 'Some' and 'Soames' echo each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene is the beautiful wife whom Soames Forsyte desires in John Galsworthy's novel sequence The Forsyte Saga.

clue.text: Habit caught in annexe

indicators.note: the cricket letter is placed inside the annexe word

parts.note: an annexe is an addition to a building
c. for caught in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: Someone's vice is discovered hidden in the extension.
explanation.walkthrough: C stands for caught on a cricket scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive dependence on something, a habit one cannot break, as in a drug habit.

clue.text: Fleming's doctor stuffs birds from an Italian port

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside a bird, so the doctor is put within the birds

parts.note: geese are birds
Dr No, the villain of Ian Fleming's Bond novel

explanation.surface: A cook stuffs poultry the way they do on the Ligurian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleming' suggests Alexander Fleming, the penicillin scientist, but it is Ian Fleming and his Dr No.
explanation.definitionFit: Genoese is the adjective for things or people belonging to Genoa, the great seaport of northwest Italy.

clue.text: New beginning after setback for family within the hour

indicators.note: a setback sends things back the way they came, so the whole combination is read backwards
within means inside, so the family word is placed inside the time word

parts.note: hr is the abbreviation for hour
a tribe is a family group or clan

explanation.surface: A family regroups after a setback, making a fresh start on the hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' looks like misfortune, but it tells you to reverse everything built from family and hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebirth is a revival or renewal, a fresh start in life, so it is a new beginning.
